title: A call under `Fun.id` (or `%identity`, an unboxed field or constructor) is not a tail call when the function allocates locally
summary: `Fun.id (loop (n - 1) (acc + 1))` as the last expression of a function that allocates on the local stack (here a comparison of two tuples) is not a tail call in native code; so is a call under `%identity`, `Obj.magic`, the field of an unboxed record or an unboxed constructor. Bytecode and OCaml 5.4.0 run it in constant stack.
cause: For the type checker the call is an argument, so it is translated with `Rc_normal`; the translation then leaves no code around it (`lambda/translprim.ml` for `%identity`, `lambda/translcore.ml` for unboxed fields and constructors), and the region is ended after the call returns.

fix.text: Gives such a call in tail position the mark that ends the region first when no argument can be local to the region (not for `Obj.magic`, nor for an unboxed constructor matched again). Builds; `test.ml` then prints the expected result; testsuite unchanged.
